subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Deployment That Skipped Staging
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Deployment That Skipped Staging usable.

hook.text: A developer pushes directly to production 'because the fix is small.' The small fix causes a two-hour outage.

buildup.text: Staging environments exist to catch problems before they reach users. Skipping them is playing with live ammunition.

discovery.text: Cloud makes it trivially easy to deploy. That ease is a double-edged sword — fast deploys mean fast disasters.

twist.text: Many of the worst cloud outages started as 'small, safe changes.' The change looked small. The blast radius wasn't.

climax.text: Guardrails — canary releases, progressive rollouts, mandatory staging — prevent small mistakes from going big.

punchline.text: The 'small fix' caused a big outage. Always use staging.

quiz.question: Why are canary releases and progressive rollouts important?
options: They catch problems with a small percentage of traffic before full deployment
They make deployments take longer, which is always safer
They are required by cloud provider terms of service

details.summary: Deploying directly to production without testing in a staging environment has caused countless incidents. Knight Capital lost $440 million in 45 minutes when untested code reached production. Staging environments exist specifically to catch issues before they affect real users.
details.whyItMatters: Every major deployment incident reinforces the same lesson: untested production deployments are high-risk gambles. Staging environments are cheap insurance against catastrophic failure.
takeaways: Knight Capital lost $440 million from an untested deployment
Staging environments catch issues before they reach users
Blue-green and canary deployments reduce production risk

faq.question: What happened at Knight Capital?
faq.answer: In 2012, Knight Capital deployed trading software to production without proper testing. Old code on one server interacted with new code, triggering millions of unintended trades in 45 minutes. The $440 million loss bankrupted the firm within days.

faq.question: What deployment strategies reduce risk?
faq.answer: Blue-green deployments run two identical environments and switch traffic after verification. Canary deployments route a small percentage of traffic to new code first. Feature flags allow code to be deployed but not activated. All reduce the blast radius of bad deployments.
